Shopify Website for a Handmade Brand: What the Store Needs

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

A handmade brand sells something a big retailer cannot: a person, a process and a point of view. A Shopify website for a handmade brand has to carry all three without getting in the way of the sale. Generic stores often miss this. They show a grid of products and a logo, and the reason someone would buy from you instead of a warehouse never appears on the page.

This guide covers the parts of a handmade store that deserve extra attention: the personality of the design, the story pages, the structure of each product page, photography, and how shoppers arrive from Pinterest. For the general basics that apply to every store, start with the Shopify website checklist and come back here for the handmade specifics.

Let the design say who made this

Personality is not decoration. It is the reason a shopper remembers you. Before you touch a theme setting, decide three things and write them down: the two or three colors that show up everywhere, the one or two fonts you will use, and the feeling you want a stranger to have in the first five seconds (cozy, bold, quiet, playful). Every page then borrows from that short list.

Handmade brands often go wrong in two opposite directions. Some cram in every color they love and look chaotic. Others strip everything back to a clean template and lose the warmth that makes the work special. A tight palette, a consistent font pair and real photos of your own work usually land in the middle. If your visual identity is still loose, sort that out first. The brand identity guide for new store owners explains why it comes before the build.

The story pages that earn trust

Shoppers buying handmade want to know who is behind the product. You do not need a long life story. You need two short pages and one small habit.

An About page with a face and a process

Say who you are, what you make, how you make it and why you started, in plain language and in your own voice. Add a photo of you or your workspace. One paragraph on materials or process is often more persuasive than a page of adjectives.

A shipping and care page

Made-to-order timing, how you package, and how to care for the item all reduce hesitation. Put the real timing here and link to it from product pages, so nobody has to guess how long a custom order takes.

A story line on every product page

One or two sentences about how that specific item is made will do more than a generic description. The brand trust guide covers more ways to show there is a real person behind the store.

A product page structure that works for handmade

Order matters on a product page. A structure that suits most handmade items looks like this:

  1. Title with the plain product name first. Say what it is before you get creative with a collection name.
  2. Price and variants near the top. Sizes, colors and personalization options should be visible without scrolling.
  3. A short paragraph on what it is and who it suits. Lead with the benefit to the buyer.
  4. Details in a list. Dimensions, materials, weight, care.
  5. Made-to-order or personalization notes. What the buyer must provide and how long it takes.
  6. Shipping and return details. Or a clear link to them.

For writing the copy itself, see how to create product listings that convert.

Photography that shows the real thing

Handmade buyers cannot touch the item, so photos do that job. Shoot one clean, well lit main image, one image for scale (in a hand, on a shelf, on a person), one close-up of texture or detail, and one that shows the item in use. Keep the background and lighting consistent across the catalog so the store looks like one brand. The product photography tips post goes deeper on lighting and angles.

Make the store findable from Pinterest

Pinterest is a visual search engine, and handmade products suit it well because people search for gift ideas, decor and styles they cannot name yet. Pins keep surfacing for months, which suits a small brand without an ad budget. For the store to benefit, product pages need descriptive titles, clear images and clean collection pages that a pin can point to. The Pinterest SEO for Shopify stores post walks through the connection, and the Pinterest guide for handmade businesses covers the pin side. No one can promise a traffic number, and results take weeks or months of steady effort.

Frequently asked questions

What should a Shopify website for a handmade brand include?

A handmade store should include a clear homepage, an About page that shows who makes the products and how, structured product pages with materials and made-to-order details, honest photography, shipping and care information, and policy pages. The personality of the brand should show in the colors, fonts and photos throughout.

Do handmade brands need a story page?

Yes, in some form. Shoppers choose handmade because a person is behind the work, so a short About page with a photo and a paragraph on your process gives them a reason to buy from you instead of a large retailer.

How many photos should a handmade product page have?

There is no fixed number, but a useful set covers a clean main image, an image that shows scale, a close-up of detail or texture and one that shows the item in use. Consistent lighting and backgrounds across the catalog make the store look like one brand.

Can Pinterest send traffic to a Shopify store for handmade products?

It can. Pinterest works like a visual search engine, and pins can keep surfacing for months. It depends on clear product pages, keyword-aware pin titles and descriptions and steady effort, and results take weeks or months rather than days.
